title: VRAM hunt: workstation repro notes
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent OOMs on dev workstation (local repro), two likely contributors: (1) driver/runtime mismatch (wheel expects newer CUDA runtime than driver supports) and/or (2) unexpected VRAM fragmentation from long-lived cache + mixed-precision allocations. This note is a command-output breadcrumb trail and hypotheses list for follow-up.

Environment snapshot (when repro happened):
- Host: ubuntu-22.04 workstation (bare metal)
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX A5000 (48GB) — but observed on smaller dev GPUs too
- Kernel: 5.15.0-70-generic
- Driver (nvidia): recorded as 510.47.03 at time A, later upgraded in tests to 535.86.05
- Python: 3.10.12 (venv)
- Torch: installed via pip wheel on 2024-12-xx (torch 2.1.0+cu118)
- conda envs also present on machine (possible PATH/LD contamination)

Commands I ran (raw):
- nvidia-smi
  -> shows Driver Version: 510.47.03, GPUs listed, some processes (chrome, vscode) occupying small mem

- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
  -> NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  510.47.03  Wed Sep  1 14:23:49 UTC 2024

- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.driver_version)"
  -> "2.1.0+cu118 True 11020" (driver_version reported as 11020 by torch api) — odd mismatch vs nvidia-smi (driver 510).

- ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch.__file__)")/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep cudart
  -> libcudart.so.11.8 => /usr/local/cuda-11.8/lib64/libcudart.so.11.8

- dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia || apt list --installed | grep cuda
  -> showed both nvidia-driver-510 and some cuda-toolkit-11-8 entries lingering from apt install history

Initial failing trace (captured from run):
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.22 GiB (GPU 0; 47.88 GiB total capacity; 46.62 GiB already allocated; 0 bytes free; 46.64 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  - happened during a batched attention step where batch size scaled up after an optimizer change

Other errors seen across trials (indicative of mismatch):
- CUDA error: driver shutting down
- ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
- CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
  - classic symptom when wheel compiled for cu118 but host driver older than runtime requirements

Hypotheses and evidence: 
1) Driver/wheel mismatch: pip wheel (cu118) expects driver >= 525.x (or at least >= 515 series for some symbols). Evidence: torch wheel references libcudart.so.11.8, ldd shows /usr/local/cuda-11.8, but system nvidia driver was 510 -> runtime complains sometimes.
2) Mixed runtime libs on LD_LIBRARY_PATH: leftover /usr/local/cuda symlinks from earlier installs causing python to bind to wrong libcudart at runtime. Evidence: ldd points to /usr/local/cuda-11.8 but apt lists old packages.
3) VRAM fragmentation + reserved blocks from previous processes/caches. Evidence: nvidia-smi shows small chrome/vscode consumer processes on GPU, but PyTorch reserved numbers are huge after repeated runs. Some experiments with torch.cuda.empty_cache() seemed to reduce immediate pressure.
4) Docker / container toolkit mismatch when reproducing inside container. Observed that running nvidia/cuda:11.7-base inside docker with host driver 510 fails with "driver insufficient" unless the container's libcudart matches host.

Mitigations / commands attempted and results: 
- pip uninstall torch && pip install --no-cache-dir torch==2.1.0+cu117 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html
  -> reduced "insufficient driver" complaints but OOMs still occurred (likely fragmentation/alloc pattern).

- sudo apt-get remove --purge 'nvidia-*' && sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-535
  -> post-upgrade, nvidia-smi reports 535.86.05. After reboot, some of the "insufficient" errors disappeared. Re-run of same workload still hit OOM at roughly same allocation point.

- Repro script: minimal_repro.py (local) run with torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high') and autocast off -> OOM persists. Lowered batch size avoids OOM (expected).

- Added tracing allocation: PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 to env -> this changes reserved numbers, OOM occurs slightly later (indicates caching plays role)

- Captured kernel logs: dmesg | grep -i nvrm / journalctl -k | grep NVRM
  -> occasional 'GPU at PCI:xxxxx: GPU page fault' entries when reproducing with multi-threaded data loader. Not stable.

- Checked for device-side asserts: set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and ran test -> previously hidden assert surfaced in one workload causing stream to abort and subsequent allocations to fail.

Reproduction notes (short recipe):
1) venv with pip torch 2.1.0+cu118 (or cu117) depending on test case
2) run minimal_repro.py with batch_size=64 and num_workers=4 for dataloader
3) run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv -l 1 in parallel to watch allocation trend
4) after ~90s, OOM thrown in forward pass at a particular attention matmul scale

Heuristics learned so far: 
- Matching driver >= wheel's minimum recommended is necessary but not sufficient. Always prefer driver >= 535 for cu118 wheels on dev machines.
- Long-running python process + many small allocations causes the CUDA caching allocator to reserve large chunks; even after torch.cuda.empty_cache(), fragmentation can remain. Restarting process frees and is often the fastest mitigation.
- LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering matters on machines with both conda and system installs. Always clear custom LD_LIBRARY_PATH when debugging or use ldd to verify resolved libs.

Open TODO / next steps: 
- [ ] Create a reproducible minimal docker image that reproduces OOM on clean host driver 535 (isolate host vs wheel issues). Add to linked PR when ready.
- [ ] Record strace + ltrace around the python process start to capture which libcudart is opened (strace -e openat -f -s 200 -o strace.out python script.py).
- [ ] Add a short bash script to atomically (1) stop GUI processes using GPU, (2) sudo systemctl stop display-manager, (3) unload nvidia modules, (4) install driver, (5) reboot — to create a reproducible clean state for testing.
- [ ] Instrument model code with torch.cuda.memory_summary() snapshots every N steps to find fragmentation point.
- [ ] Follow-up with infra to add a daily CI smoke that runs the minimal_repro on smallest allowed GPU to catch regressions early (linked JIRA above).

Notes for whoever picks this up:
- If you see "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" -> first check nvidia-smi driver number vs wheel target, then check ldd on libtorch_cuda.so.
- If you see 'libcudart.so.11.8 not found' -> check /usr/local/cuda-11.8/* and any conda-installed cudatoolkit packages.
- Use NVPROF / Nsight when you have a stable repro (OOM makes profiling noisy).

Recent quick wins:
- Upgrading to driver 535 removed the mismatch errors entirely on my machine.
- Setting num_workers=0 in dataloader eliminated sporadic page-fault kernel log entries (race in worker init) — reduced instability during long runs.

Misc raw snippets I captured: 
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 4.00 GiB (GPU 0; 15.90 GiB total capacity; 7.12 GiB already allocated; 8.78 GiB free; 9.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" (triggered when running an older driver with cu118-built wheel)
- nvidia-smi (before): Driver Version: 510.47.03, CUDA Version: 11.6
- nvidia-smi (after): Driver Version: 535.86.05, CUDA Version: 12.1

If anything above is inconsistent or you reproduce a different trace, paste full outputs here and I'll update. This file is a working breadcrumb log — feel free to copy, extend, or redact for tickets.

-- Arielle
